content:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: prod-east GPU pool showing sustained queue growth and throttling > 90% for text-gen. Autoscaler failing to provision new nodes (error: placement_failed). Paging @sarah (on-call)

sarah: on it. hitting the incident channel. can someone paste the autoscaler logs + prometheus graphs?

jia: grabbing graphs now — queue length up to 18k reqs, 99th latency spiking to 12s, token throughput flat. embedding and rerank unaffected.

jia: prom snippets:
```
prod_inference_request_queue_length{region="prod-east"} 18023
prod_gpu_utilization{node_pool="gpu-prod-east"} 92.1
redwood_autoscaler_failed_scales_total{reason="placement_failed"} 7
```

leo: looked at cluster autoscaler events — placement failed because nodes with free GPU memory exist but not the right MIG slice sizes. Got lots of small pods requesting 1g-MIG and a bunch of 4g-MIG nodes. Fragmentation -> stranded vGPU capacity.

leo: pasted node describe for one node:
```
Name: gpu-node-12
Allocatable: nvidia.com/mig-1g: 0, nvidia.com/mig-2g: 2
Allocated: nvidia.com/mig-1g: 4, nvidia.com/mig-2g: 0
Events:
  Warning  FailedPlacement  10m (x5)  cluster-autoscaler  cannot find nodes for pod: insufficient gpu_mig_1g
```

ops_lead: confirmed. autoscaler tries to spin new nodes but cluster-level quota + fragmentation prevents scheduling. We have ~3 stranded MIGs (small slices) on nodes but pods want different slice sizes.

sam: any immediate customer impact?

customer_success: mapped top queue owners — two customers on dedicated reserved pools impacted (acct-042, acct-110), plus several self-serve customers hitting hosted API fallbacks. CS is notifying acct-042 as high.

jia: mitigation options I see:
- rebalance pods to force binpacking (cordon/drain specific nodes)
- temporarily allow mixed MIG sizing by changing pod requests to be flexible (not quick)
- force reconfigure nodes to consolidate MIG slices (requires drain + reboot)
- enable fallback routing to smaller models to reduce GPU load (fastest)

sarah: prioritize minimal-customer-impact quickest path. deploy fallback routing to smaller model version for non-enterprise customers, and start manual node rebalancing for reserved pools.

leo: starting manual rebalancing: will cordon nodes with fragmented small slices to consolidate workloads onto nodes with larger contiguous MIGs. Commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

leo: also going to restart the nvidia-device-plugin daemonset after drains to ensure MIG advertising is correct: `kubectl rollout restart ds/nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system`

jia: I'm deploying a routing patch now to send non-sla customers to smaller-llama-7b-fp16. config snippet:
```
routing:
  - match: "customer_tier != enterprise"
    route_to: llama-7b-fp16-fallback
    weight: 100
```

deploybot: deploy started for routing config (deploy id: d-8812).

sam: ticketing: opening incident->customer-impact doc, assigning follow-ups.

leo: note: autoscaler also hit GCE quota for GPUs in prod-east when attempting to spin 3 nodes at once; I requested temporary quota bump with cloud team.

ops_lead: good. timeline: routing change should reduce immediate GPU pressure. manual drains will take ~30-45m. CS, keep customers updated.

customer_success: notified acct-042: they see elevated latency and some 503s; they've acknowledged. CS will escalate if they report revenue impact.

jia: routing deploy complete. metrics: within 6m, queue dropped from 18k -> 8k — immediate relief for hosted customers.

leo: drain/cordon in progress. encountered one stuck pod that kept restarting due to `OOMKilled` on small-slice images; handled with `kubectl delete pod` and recreating on larger node.

leo: restarted device plugin, re-advertised MIG sizes. After that, autoscaler was able to schedule 2 new nodes with compatible MIG configs.

deploybot: cloud quota bump confirmed (temporary) — requested by leo, approved.

jia: autoscaler logs after changes:
```
I1123 14:22:10 autoscaler.go: new nodes requested: 2
I1123 14:25:48 autoscaler.go: nodes provisioned: gpu-node-33,gpu-node-34
I1123 14:26:05 scheduler.go: placed 42 pending pods
```

jia: queue now 900, overall 99th latency down to 3.2s. throttling reduced to 6%.

ops_lead: are there still stranded vGPUs? any residual fragmentation?

leo: one rack still has mismatched MIG topology causing 1 stranded 1g slice. I'll schedule a maintenance window to reprovision MIG shapes overnight. Not blocking production now.

sarah: handing off on-call to jia for the night. jia will own remediation steps and follow-ups. @jia you good?

jia: oncall acked. I'll monitor for 2 hours then file a full postmortem.

sam: post-incident actions (quick):
- triage MIG sizing policy and pod request validation (owner: leo)
- add a scheduler predicate to detect fragmentation and prefer binpacking (owner: eng-runtime)
- ensure autoscaler retries don't get blocked by temporary quota failures (owner: infra)
- update runbook for fallback routing (owner: product)

customer_success: acct-042 confirmed latency improving. they'll continue to monitor.

incident-bot: P1 -> P2 at 2027-01-23T14:40:00Z (manual). All major queues back to nominal.

jia: we'll run a full RCA tomorrow. Notes to include: MIG fragmentation + autoscaler interaction + cloud quota boundary + lack of runtime fragmentation awareness.

leo: will capture `nvidia-smi` and MIG configs from affected nodes and attach to ticket.

sarah: thanks team. leave channel open for another hour then archive. :white_check_mark:
